answer_1.quote: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enables large language models (LLMs) to access and reason over external knowledge by retrieving relevant documents and conditioning generation on them.

answer_2.quote: We measure performance using Generation Accuracy, which combines a fast span-matching test with a lightweight LLM-based correctness check.

answer_3.quote: If the span check fails, this fallback invokes a frozen LLM to assess whether the prediction semantically entails any gold answer. The LLM is prompted to respond with a binary judgment ("yes" or "no").

answer_4.quote: To assess the alignment of our primary evaluation metric, Generation Accuracy, with human judgment, we conducted a human annotation study. We randomly sampled 1,000 answer generations from the general-domain QA test set. Each sample was labeled as Correct (1) or Incorrect (0) by human annotators...
answer_4.guideline: You are an evaluator for question-answering systems. Your task is to determine whether the system-generated answer aligns with the provided gold (reference) answers. Evaluation Criteria: An answer should be marked as correct (1) if it: • Contains the same key information as the golden answers; • Expresses the same meaning, even if using different wording; • Is factually consistent with the golden answers.
